chapter: Postwar Chicago, Janis and De Paris
title: Brief dance tour with Jelly Roll Morton
summary: About three weeks with Morton's eleven- or twelve-piece band in Florida and the East, for about $40.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Now, it says here on the liner notes to the Circle album, Conrad Janis and His Tailgate Jazz Band... It says here: "Drummer Freddie Moore, who once played with King Oliver and Jelly Roll, volunteered. This was for the recording session under Rudi Blesh with Conrad Janis as the leader. Now, before we get to your volunteering, you did a few dates, you say, with Jelly Roll Morton. Just scattered, they didn't last a long time.
Mmm-hmm.
Okay. Now, you volunteered. In other words, you were, I guess, enthusiastic about making the record, and that's why you volunteered to make the recording with Conrad Janis?
Yeah, Conrad Janis, but this other guy, what name is that...?
Blesh? Oh, Sharpstein? Bob Green...
[PAUSE]
See, Jelly Roll Morton was only for just a few weeks. We did a tour, what's called a dance tour down in Florida, and so forth. That was after(?) ...(?)., played
Moore (III) - 65
concert dances. I think he around about an eleven- or twelve-piece band, twelve pieces in his band. But he didn't do so hot with his band -- you know, traveling.
Was that before you joined King Oliver that you were with Jelly? Or was this afterwards?
I think that was before King Oliver. No, maybe not. I came to New York in 1928. I recorded in '29, '30... It must have been after
After King Oliver.
Yes.
[PAUSE]

I'm talking about these dates with Jelly Roll Morton that you did. And you said he had about an eleven-piece band, and he wrote out...he would write out his pieces with the parts for the musicians and so forth. But you didn't play a great deal, any long time with him. It was just some scattered dates. And you mentioned Florida and Philadelphia, apparently, for Jelly Roll Morton -- the few times that you played with Jelly Roll.

I was with Jelly Roll I'd say about three weeks altogether. Because he played with his dance band down in Florida, in Miami. There was some across Virginia, some across Pennsylvania. [INAUDIBLE SENTENCE]
Moore (III) - 66
How was he...? Who was managing him at that time?
I think he did his own managing. I think it was him.
And you made... Even though you were with him three weeks, you made pretty good money at that time?
Yeah. I made around forty dollars. During that time, that was a minimum, you know. If you made forty dollars, you're doing good, you know, during that time.
